title: Fix crash on closed generic structs from referenced assemblies

lines.text: Learn more about using a mix of your own custom formatters and automatically generated ones in [the Analyzer section](#analyzer).

Closed generic types defined in a referenced assembly (for example, `Item<int>` where `Item<T>` is defined in another project or NuGet package) can be used as members of your `[MessagePackObject]` types, including generic value types and record structs.
Diagnostics about the members of such a type are reported by the assembly that defines it rather than by the consuming project, so any problem must be fixed there.

[MagicOnion](https://github.com/Cysharp/MagicOnion) is a code-first gRPC framework based on grpc-dotnet and MessagePack. gRPC usually communicates with Protocol Buffers using IDL. But MagicOnion uses MessagePack for C# and does not need IDL. When communicating C# to C#, schemaless (or rather C# classes as schema) is better than using IDL.
This analyzer only reports on members declared in the project being compiled.
Members of a type defined in a referenced assembly are reported by the project that defines that type, so an unattributed public member of such a type must be fixed in its defining project.

requirement.title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement.intent: A [MessagePackObject] type with a member whose type is a closed generic value type from a referenced assembly must build cleanly and still get a generated resolver.

functional.text: The generator does not throw when a member's type is a closed generic struct or record struct defined in a referenced assembly.
The analyzer does not throw for the same member types.
The compiling assembly gets its generated resolver, as it does when the generic type is declared in the same project.

nonFunctional.text: A failure of the generator or analyzer must not pass silently as a build warning that leaves the assembly without a resolver. (inferred)
Behaviour for generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same project does not change. (inferred)

story.what: TypeCollector no longer indexes DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] when it builds the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull and field MemberNeedsKey diagnostics. Instead it uses null-safe lookups, so a symbol from metadata (no syntax) yields a null location. The collector's report callback is now wrapped so that only diagnostics located in a syntax tree of the current compilation are forwarded. The analyzer now starts TypeCollector only for [MessagePackObject] classes, not structs. New tests compile a defining assembly to a metadata-only reference, run the analyzer and generator on a consuming project, and check that the resolver is generated with no warnings. README and MsgPack004 docs explain that diagnostics for such types belong to the defining assembly.
story.why: Requirement MP-2283: a closed generic struct or record struct from a referenced assembly, used as a member type, made the generator and analyzer throw IndexOutOfRangeException. The symbol has no syntax, so DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] failed. As a result the build gave only crash warnings and the assembly had no generated resolver.

New helper that reports a diagnostic only when its location is in a syntax tree of the compilation.
New harness plus three metadata-reference tests for a struct, a record struct and an unkeyed member.

findings.title: Analyzer no longer validates [MessagePackObject] structs
findings.detail: AnalyzeSymbol used to call TypeCollector.Collect for Class or Struct types that carry [MessagePackObject]. Now it only does so for Class. The symbol action only fires for types declared in the compilation, so this change does nothing for referenced-assembly types (the reported scenario). Its only effect is that every [MessagePackObject] struct declared in the user's own project stops being analyzed. Those structs will no longer get MsgPack004 (missing Key), MsgPack005 (duplicate or mixed keys), MsgPack007, MsgPack011, MsgPack015 or MsgPack017. Invalid structs then compile without errors and fail or misbehave only at generation or run time. The requirement does not ask for this, and it breaks N2 (behaviour for non-generic structs and same-project types must not change).

findings.title: Location filter silently drops real problems in source types
findings.detail: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation discards every diagnostic whose location is not in source, including Location.None. Several call sites can produce a null location for a member that really is declared in the project. Example: a positional record property with [Key(null)]. Its declaring syntax is a ParameterSyntax, so GetPropertyIdentifierLocation returns null and BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull is thrown away. CheckValidMessagePackFormatterAttribute can also produce a null location. Before the change these problems were reported (or crashed). Now they vanish with no diagnostic, so an invalid type in the user's own project builds cleanly. This goes against N1 (failures must not pass silently) and N2. The filter should only drop diagnostics whose symbol comes from metadata, or fall back to the symbol's source location instead of dropping.

findings.title: MsgPack004 doc contradicts base-type member reporting
findings.detail: The new note says MsgPack004 only reports members declared in the project being compiled, and that unattributed members of a referenced-assembly type must be fixed in the defining project. That is not what the analyzer does. When a source type derives from a base type in a referenced assembly that has unattributed public members, TypeCollector still reports BaseTypeContainsUnattributedPublicMembers (MsgPack004) at the base type reference in the consuming project, and that location passes the new filter. The help page therefore misdescribes when MsgPack004 fires.

citations.quote: This analyzer only reports on members declared in the project being compiled.

findings.title: No check of generated resolver content or round-trip
findings.detail: F3 requires the consuming assembly to get its resolver and formatters as it would for a same-project generic struct. The new tests set SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck and only assert that a source with the resolver hint name exists. They do not check that the resolver registers the formatter for MyObject or the closed generic MyGenericStruct<int> / Item<int>, and they have no snapshot under Resources. No runtime test round-trips such a value through the generated resolver. If the resolver were generated but left out the generic formatter, every new test would still pass.

findings.title: No test with the referenced generic struct as a field
findings.detail: F1 covers members in general, and the expectation names the field case explicitly. All three new tests use the referenced closed generic only as a property type of the consuming object. None declares a field of type MyGenericStruct<int> or Item<int>, which goes through the separate IFieldSymbol collection loop.
